title: France Caught in a Fiscal Trap as Growth Falters and Households Feel the… · 16 Sep
keywords: France, fiscal deficit, eurozone, budget consolidation, economic growth, household spending, inflation, European Commission, Banque de France, sovereign debt, French politics, austerity, consumer confidence, EU fiscal rules
notes: France is facing a convergence of weak economic growth, a stubbornly high budget deficit, and exhausted consumers, creating a political and economic bind with few easy exits. The European Commission projects the French deficit at around 5.1 percent of GDP in 2026, well above the EU's three percent ceiling, while the Banque de France sees growth of just 0.5 percent that same year. With fiscal consolidation, household fatigue, and institutional distrust colliding simultaneously, Paris faces choices that are costly whichever path it takes.
